key_concepts: Electric circuits consist of a source, connecting wires, and a load or device
A series circuit has only one path or loop for current
A parallel circuit gives each device its own separate path or branch
Schematic diagrams use symbols to represent circuit components
In a series circuit, current is the same through all components
In a series circuit, total voltage is the sum of individual voltages
In a series circuit, total resistance is the sum of individual resistances
In a parallel circuit, total current is the sum of branch currents
In a parallel circuit, voltage is the same across each branch
In a parallel circuit, total resistance is less than the smallest branch resistance
A burnt-out bulb in a series circuit stops current in the entire circuit
Parallel connections allow appliances to operate independently
